thread:
Aria Li: quick question for the RFC follow-up: should we ban wildcard-scoped API keys (org:*) by default? customers love them for convenience but they complicate revocation and telemetry.
Marcus Reed: prefer to discourage default use. wildcard keys are fine short-term but dangerous long-term. propose making them require an explicit org-admin opt-in and extra audit.
Gwen Thomas: product tradeoff: PLG onboarding friction vs security. maybe allow wildcard keys but tag them and surface usage in Console with tighter rate limits. also provide one-click narrow conversion (split key by project).
Omar Said: engineering: wildcard scope blows out policy bundle size if we try to materialize perms. better keep runtime tokens minimal and treat wildcard keys as legacy that broker mints ephemeral tokens for.
Aria Li: migration plan idea: 1) detect org:* key usage, 2) broker issues ephemeral rid-scoped token when used (with short TTL), 3) email admins + console banner recommending split, 4) after 6 months, deny new org:* creations unless approved.
Marcus Reed: also surface risky routes that were invoked with wildcard keys so customers can prioritize splitting. make this an automated report.
Gwen Thomas: for Dedicated/Private: allow org:* but require offline policy bundle in agent and admin confirmation. document that revocation window is bounded by token TTL + bundle refresh.
auth-bot: runbook note added: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/wildcard-keys (task: "org-wildcard-migration-report")
Aria Li: action items: Marcus write opt-in policy & console banner text, Gwen design the split-key UX, Omar add broker flow + audit event prototype. sync Thurs 2pm to finalize RFC appendix.
